series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 1/3] mm: swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator. The swap cache allocator is used by zswap writeback to allocate a folio that can be freed directly once writeback completes, without being on the LRU. This change allows for more flexibility in managing swap cache folios and prevents potential issues with synchronous devices or asynchronous ones. The patch updates several files, including mm/swap.h and mm/swap_state.c, to reflect this change.

review_comments.author: Kunwu Chan
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that the new allocator contract is preserved by all callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(), but pointed out a minor consistency issue in swapfile.c referencing the old function name.
review_comments.raw_body:
I checked the callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(). The regular 
swap-in paths add the folio to the LRU after allocation, while 
the zswap writeback path keeps it off-LRU for the dropbehind 
handling in patch 3. 
The new allocator contract is preserved by all callers.

swapfile.c still references the old name in a comment \u2014 minor
consistency nit.

Reviewed-by: Kunwu Chan <kunwu.chan@gmail.com>

Thanks,
KunWu

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 2/3] mm: swap: drop dropbehind swap cache folios on writeback completion
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the Linux kernel to drop swap cache folios from their cache once writeback completes, rather than leaving them for reclaim to find later. This is achieved by setting a flag on the write operation and dropping the folio directly in the folio_end_writeback() function. The change extends existing functionality for file folios to also include swap cache folios. The patch modifies several kernel files, including mm/filemap.c, mm/page_io.c, mm/swap_state.c, and mm/vmscan.c.

review_comments.author: Kunwu Chan
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Kunwu Chan confirmed that the refcount handoff from folio_end_writeback() to swap_writeback_dropbehind_folio() is correct, providing an extra reference for remove_mapping_reclaim(), and ensuring the folio remains alive across a racing swapin.
sentiment_signals: no specific concerns or objections raised
review_comments.raw_body:
I checked the refcount handoff from folio_end_writeback() to
swap_writeback_dropbehind_folio(): the extra reference provides the
expected caller reference for remove_mapping_reclaim(), giving the
expected 1 + folio_nr_pages(folio) count for folio_ref_freeze().

The swapcache/dropbehind state is sampled before clearing PG_writeback,
and the extra reference keeps the folio alive across a racing swapin.

Reviewed-by: Kunwu Chan <kunwu.chan@gmail.com>

Thanks,
KunWu

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 3/3] mm: zswap: drop cold writeback folios via swap dropbehind
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the zswap writeback process by dropping cold folios from the swap cache after they are written back to disk, rather than leaving them on the LRU for reclaim. This is done by allocating the folio off the LRU and marking it PG_dropbehind, which allows the swap dropbehind path to free the folio once writeback completes. The patch aims to reduce memory residency time for cold pages and improve system performance.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series improves the performance of zswap by promptly freeing cold writeback folios instead of leaving them on the LRU for page reclaim to find and free later. The existing dropbehind mechanism is extended to swap cache folios, allowing zswap to opt into it. This change reduces memory residency and waste in reclaim scans. Patch 1 moves LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator, patch 2 drops dropbehind swap cache folios on writeback completion, and patch 3 enables zswap to allocate its writeback folio off the LRU and mark it as dropbehind.
